svg.font-family: Inter, 'IBM Plex Sans', 'Segoe UI', system-ui, sans-serif
svg.title: How every lane is checked
svg.desc: Six layers of checks. Unit tests compare every lane with StrictMath at 128, 256 and 512 bits, masked and unmasked. Hard cases come from Lefevre's tables, CORE-MATH's lists and exact cases computed here. Planted faults must each be caught. CI reads the machine code of every arm and checks allocation. A nightly sweep and fuzz run on x86 and Arm. Lemmas cover only the places where a port computes differently from the C, parts of some machine-checked.
svg.text: How every lane is checked
Six layers, each against StrictMath or against the machine code; none of them alone is the proof.
Unit tests at every width
Each lane against StrictMath by raw bits, at every width the host has (128,
256, 512 bits, the preferred species), masked and unmasked. mvn -B verify
Hard cases
Inputs whose exact result lies near a rounding boundary: Lefèvre's tables,
CORE-MATH's MIT lists for hypot and pow, and exact cases computed for both.
Planted faults must be caught
Deliberate bugs (a dropped term, a moved threshold), each switched on in a
JVM of its own; the check named for it must fail. -Dvfdlibm.fault=…
CI reads the machine code
C2's code of every arm: the width's registers, no fused multiply-add, from 256
bits up no call but the JIT's traps; and an allocation check for boxed bodies.
Every night, on x86 and Arm
A sweep of all 2^32 high words, three low words each, and a fuzz from a fresh
seed at every width; x86's 128 bits a 1/32 slice a night. A failure opens an issue.
Lemmas only where a port departs from the C
Numbered in PROOFS.md with the test of their hypotheses; parts of those for
exp, log and expm1 are machine-checked by Z3 and cvc5 (proofs/).
Everywhere else, the port is fdlibm's C, operation by operation, and the tests compare it with StrictMath.
